anti_overlap: Leave WRITTEN INSTRUMENTS, POSTED BONDS, SURETIES, COURTS, AND NEGOTIATED CUSTODY to fd-prize-court-commission-capture. Do not propose a standing commission, a bond posted in advance with a known amount, a third-party adjudicator, condemnation proceedings, or prisoner-cartel/ransom/parole machinery — and specifically do not reach for the jirga's security deposit, which is the one bond-shaped object in this domain and belongs to that lens. This order has no writing and no enforcer at all: its restraint instrument is self-judgment (an unknown amount, conceded after the fact, paid to the victim rather than to a court) and its account of captured is a set of live claims held by parties who cannot compel each other, not a negotiated custody economy. Where the two converge on 'captured needs verbs', contribute only the two-claimant conflict and the transferable claim.

Leave TESTIMONY, PROVENANCE, CHAIN GRADING, AND REPORT RELIABILITY to fd-isnad-report-chain-integrity. Do not grade reports, propose corroboration, split integrity from precision, or build falsity detection. This lens's epistemic position is the opposite one and must be framed as such: attribution is a decision the injured party makes and enforces, not a finding derived from evidence, and it is fully effective while wrong. If a finding starts to be about whether something can be known or believed on evidence, stop and hand it over.

Leave EMPLOYER ECONOMICS, UNDIRECTED MONEY, PURCHASED EXPERTISE, CUTOUTS, AND DENIABILITY-AS-LIFESTYLE to fd-gibson-employer-handler. This order has no employer and no money that launders anything — payment here is a public tariff everyone knows in advance, which is the opposite of undirected funding. Its account of what holds a person is a third party's claim, not a dyadic psychological hold, and its account of deniability is that it is an aggravating condition rather than a status you live inside.

Leave KLEPT, STUBS, AUNTIES, CAPTURE-WEIGHTING, BODY ECONOMIES, AND FOUND-OBJECT INTELLIGENCE to fd-gibson-tradecraft-orgshapes. Kin appears in both lenses and the boundary must be stated explicitly in any finding that touches it: there, kin is capture leverage the player exploits to reach a power bloc (f-030); here, kin is a co-liable claimant who can indict the ORG. Do not propose family capture-weighting, patriarch keys, or bloc formation.

Leave THE OPPOSING SERVICE, THE STANDING LICENSE, THE QUARTERMASTER, STATION CHIEFS, AND SAFEHOUSES to fd-fleming-bond-oversight. Do NOT build a rival organization or a counterintelligence layer — the entire contribution of this lens to that cluster is that a distributed web of individually weak claims, held by parties with no budget, no coordination, and no strategy, generates adversarial exposure more cheaply than a mirror service and can be wrong in ways a designed adversary cannot. Argue that comparison explicitly rather than proposing an org.

Leave THE PRE-ORDER CONDITION REGIME, THE IRREVERSIBLE RELEASE, THE NAMED DIVERGENCE BEHAVIOURS, THE BRIEFING-DEPTH DIAL, AND THE CLOSING RECOVERY WINDOW to fd-falconry-conditioned-release. Do not propose condition management, weight/stress regimes, hooding, or a decay clock on capture. Both lenses supply a claimant for the captured operative and the difference must be named: falconry's claimant acquires by feeding, so capture is a race against a closing window; this lens's claimant holds a priced claim that can be settled, sold, refused, or inherited, so capture is a reckoning with no clock. Contribute only the reckoning.

Leave THE INSTRUMENT-VERSUS-CONDITION TENSION to fd-fused-standing-tie-instrument-versus-condition. Do not re-argue either parent's half. This lens exists to supply a third position both parents structurally exclude — the unrecorded act is neither merely unaccounted nor safely deniable, because attribution happens anyway, by decision rather than by evidence, and lands on a group. Say so once, then work from it.

Do not re-derive the doc's own comparables (MGSV Mother Base, XCOM, RimWorld/DF, Darkest Dungeon, CK3) or restate §1's measured grounding as findings — the doc already made those arguments and this run has already mined its source fictions. Every finding must be traceable to something this order knows that game-design comparables and the seven covered lenses cannot reach.
decision_lens: Judge the doc the way an elder judges a house's conduct over a season — not by what they intended, but by what is owed, to whom, and whether any of it can ever be cleared. FIRST, find every place the doc treats non-attribution as an unqualified benefit, and say plainly what this order says instead: the concealed act is the unatonable one. Read §5.1's deniability gap and ask what verb, anywhere in the document, ever clears a grievance the org has caused. If the answer is none, then the doc has built an economy in which liability only accumulates, and its most 'deniable' player is its most indebted, and its scoring reads that player as clean. Then check whether the fix is small: a flag recording whether the org avowed an op, plus a settlement path only avowed acts can enter, is one field and one verb, and it converts deniability from a free good into a priced choice — which is exactly the unfakeable restraint signal this run has been hunting since f-016. SECOND, test attribution. The doc's `exposed` means the operative's identity is known and it is always correct. Ask what represents a third party BELIEVING the org acted, whether or not it did, and acting on that belief. Argue explicitly that an attribution field on a grievance is the cheapest possible answer to this run's twice-converged missing-counterparty cluster, and say why it is better than an opposing service for a kernel: it needs no strategy, no budget, no roster, and no AI, and it can be wrong, which a modelled rival service designed to be a fair adversary generally cannot. THIRD, look for the third party. The dossier problem this run already found (the operative's record can only ever indict the operative) is unfixable from inside the operative's record; ask whether the operative arrives attached to anyone — kin, house, patron, the group that vouched — who is jointly liable for them and jointly entitled against the org. Prefer the version that puts the counter-sign outside the cadre record. FOURTH, test every terminal state for claims. `dead`, `captured`, `exposed`, `burned` should each generate specific claims held by specific parties, and at least one of those claims should be the org's own. A terminal state that produces only a roster hole fails the doc's own echo ruler and should be named as failing it. FIFTH, ask whether the org can be publicly shamed. `burn` and `cut loose` are private in §4.1/§4.2; ask what third parties observe and how it changes their behaviour, and specifically whether the network's recruitment prices should read the org's record of honouring versus repudiating. SIXTH, count the inbound verbs. If the answer is zero, that is a structural finding, not a wish-list item. SEVENTH, price collateral harm in-world: `no-collateral` is a constraint on the order, not a debt in the world, and a public tariff is what makes restraint legible without any adjudicator. PREFER any proposal that (a) is one field or one flag rather than an apparatus, (b) uses parties the world already contains rather than inventing an organization, (c) produces a distinguishably different world under the doc's own echo ruler, and (d) can be placed with a ring, a build step, and which of {order contract, bench scoring hooks, loss spectrum, build plan} it changes. REJECT — explicitly, against yourself — any proposal that requires modelling kinship graphs or genealogies across 218 countries; any escalation mechanic with no termination condition, because an unbounded feud spiral is correct in the tradition and unplayable as a game; and any proposal that treats a living tradition as costume, maps a real people onto a game faction, or imports a documented abuse of these systems (compensation paid in persons) as a mechanic — name that rail once and hold it.
distance_rationale: This is the only major order-and-obligation system that has none of the apparatus every covered lens depends on. It has no writing, no state, no standing authority, no court of record, no adjudicator with power to enforce, no salaried service, no employer, no money-as-laundering, no equipment economy, no testimony-grading, and no animal husbandry. What it has instead is a fully worked-out, centuries-tested account of what happens when harm occurs and nobody can compel anything: liability is collective and attaches to a group, attribution is a decision the injured party makes and acts on whether or not it is correct, settlement is voluntary and priced by tariff, and the only sanction is the credible expectation that someone whose duty it is will answer. That gives it a native and mechanically cheap answer to the two clusters this run has converged on twice each and left unsolved — the absent Ring 3 counterparty (f-011/f-018) and the verbless captured/exposed terminal states (f-012/f-017) — without building the mirror organization Fleming reaches for or the negotiated custody economy prize law reaches for. Its sharpest and most alien contribution is a direct inversion of the doc's central premise: in this order, concealing your authorship of a harm is not a shield but an aggravator. An announced killing (víg) is a debt with a price and a settlement path; a concealed one (morð) is unatonable and permanently poisons the parties. A principal who is deniable about everything is not clean, it is the most indebted actor in the world, because it has forfeited every route to clearing anything. That reading is unreachable from all seven covered lenses: prize law says the unrecorded act is merely unaccounted, Gibson says the unrecorded tie IS the deniability apparatus, and the fused lens holds exactly that tension — this lens supplies a third position both parents structurally exclude, that the unrecorded act is neither unaccounted nor deniable but attributed anyway, by the injured, to whoever they believe did it, and enforceable while wrong. It is pre-modern, largely non-Western, contains no AI-cliche domain (no ecology, immune system, market, jazz, chess, orchestra, gardening, or city planning), and its unit of analysis — a named group of tens to thousands of people who owe and are owed — sits at exactly the scale the doc's two-tier roster occupies.
expected_isomorphisms: VÍG VERSUS MORÐ (an announced killing is prosecutable and payable at a tariff; a concealed one is morð — shameful, unatonable, and outside the settlement system entirely) maps to the doc's unexamined premise that non-attribution is a free good. §5.1 prices only the gap between order and outcome; nothing anywhere in §4–§7 prices the fact that an unavowed harm can never be settled, so a maximally deniable org accumulates permanent, unclearable grievance while scoring as clean. The cheap fix is one boolean on the op record — did the org avow authorship — plus a settlement path that only avowed harms can enter. That makes deniability a choice with a downstream price rather than pure upside, and makes AVOW a restraint signal a uniformly-vague Bigend-style principal cannot fake, because avowal is costly, irreversible, and independent of order wording (directly attacks the ceiling-pegged c-deniability-gap-vague-employer-saturation cluster from an angle no covered lens holds).

ATTRIBUTION AS A SOCIAL ACT BY THE INJURED (the mag group or the house decides who is answerable and acts on that decision; misattributed feud is common, and being wrongly blamed costs exactly what being rightly blamed costs) maps to the doc's `exposed` state, which is binary, always correct, and always about the operative's identity. There is no state in which a third party BELIEVES your org did something — correctly or not — and acts accordingly. One `attributed_to` field on a grievance is an adversarial exposure generator that needs no opposing organization, no counterintelligence service, and no rival sponsor: the world blames someone, sometimes you, sometimes wrongly, and behaves differently. This is the kernel-scale answer to c-opposing-org-absent that Fleming's mirror-service answer cannot be.

COLLECTIVE LIABILITY AND THE VOUCHING GROUP (a person is a member of a mag/jilib/house that is jointly liable for what they do and jointly entitled to claim against whoever harms them; you contract with the group, not the individual) maps directly onto f-038's single-signed dossier problem, and supplies the counter-sign from OUTSIDE the operative rather than inside them. The operative arrives attached to a third party that holds a standing claim against the org — so `hire` is a contract with a group, `burn` may default on that group, and the org becomes an indictable party in the same currency as everyone else, without inventing an org-side obligation ledger the cadre record has to carry.

MANBOT — THE TWO-CLAIMANT PROBLEM (when a man is killed, bot is owed to his kin and manbot separately to the lord who lost his service; the two claims are distinct, can conflict, and are settled separately) maps to what `dead`, `captured`, and `exposed` currently produce: a roster hole and a note. Feud law says a lost operative generates at least two live claims held by different parties with different interests, and the org holds one of them — meaning the org has a verb available (press the claim, sell it, forgo it) that the doc does not have, and the operative's kin have one against the org if the org's order is what killed them.

SJÁLFDÆMI — SELF-JUDGMENT (the wrongdoer concedes to the injured party the right to name their own compensation, amount unknown in advance) maps to a restraint verb that is structurally unfakeable: the player submits to a price they do not control. This is not a posted bond — the amount is unknown, it is paid after the fact, and it goes to the victim rather than to a court — which makes it the one restraint signal in this whole run that survives a principal whose orders are all vague by design, since it is an act rather than a wording.

THE GRIEVANCE AS A TRANSFERABLE ASSET (an Icelandic killing-case could be sold or given to a more powerful man who had the standing to prosecute it) maps to how a counterparty EMERGES rather than being authored: unsettled grievances against the org accumulate as individually weak claims held by scattered parties, and a strong actor acquires and consolidates them. The opposing organization the doc lacks becomes an emergent consequence of the player's own unsettled record rather than a designed adversary — which is both cheaper and a better fit for the doc's kernel discipline.

OUTLAWRY VERSUS PRIVATE SEVERANCE (skóggangr/fjörbaugsgarðr is a public declaration that a person is outside protection, and it works because every third party changes behaviour toward them) maps to `burn` and `cut loose`, which in §4.1/§4.2 are private acts with an attachment cost and no world echo. Public repudiation is the version that passes the echo ruler, and it has a reciprocal the doc has no room for at all: an org with a record of repudiating its own people is one the network prices differently at `recruit`.

BESA / TRYGGÐ / TEEGA — THE TRUCE WITH A CLOCK (a sworn cessation for a stated term, purchasable through mediators, catastrophically expensive to break) maps to a settle/truce verb on an exposure or grievance track: a spend that buys a bounded pause rather than a reduction, and whose breach costs far more than the original harm. It gives the exposure economy something other than accumulation and decay.

NANAWATAI / GRIÐR — SANCTUARY THAT CANNOT BE REFUSED (a supplicant, including an enemy, who comes to your door must be received, and refusing is a public disgrace) maps to a structural absence: every verb in all three rings is player-initiated. The world never asks the player for anything. An inbound request — a compromised asset, a burned operative's kin, a mediator's approach — is a verb class the doc has zero instances of, and it is where obligation becomes felt rather than accounted.

THE MEDIATOR WITH NO POWER (jirga elders, ndërmjetës, oday — they propose, they cannot enforce, and their own standing is spent on whether the proposal is accepted) maps to a second, non-tilt use for network assets: spend an asset's standing to broker a settlement, at risk to the asset. §6.2 currently gives the network exactly one output (institutional tilt); this is a second one that costs the same currency and produces a different world.

TARIFFS BY RANK (every injury has a price, scaled by who was hurt; the schedule is public and everybody knows it) maps to the `no-collateral` constraint, which is currently a scoring abstraction with no in-world counterpart. A public price list turns collateral harm into a specific, named, owed, accruing debt to a specific party — which is what makes restraint legible without any adjudicator at all.

BLOOD DOES NOT AGE (an unsettled claim is cleared by payment or by an answering act, never by the passage of time) maps to a question the doc never asks: does exposure decay? If it does, every restraint decision is temporary and the long-run optimum is to absorb and wait; if it does not, the org needs a clearing verb, which it currently lacks entirely.
focus: Whether the doc has mistaken deniability for a free good. In a system with no state and no court, concealing authorship does not reduce your liability — it removes the only route by which liability can ever be discharged, and the injured party attributes the harm to somebody regardless, correctly or not, and acts on it. Test §5.1's deniability apparatus, §4.1's loss spectrum, and Ring 3's exposure economy against that inversion: is there any verb that clears a grievance; is there any state in which the world blames the org for something (rightly or wrongly); does the operative come attached to any third party that holds a claim against the org; do `burn` and `cut loose` have public consequences or only private costs; is there a price list for collateral harm; does exposure age; and is there a single inbound verb anywhere in the three rings. Every finding must name its ring, say whether it changes the order contract, the bench scoring hooks, the loss spectrum, or the build plan, and — since §9 steps 1–3 are explicitly restricted to routing machinery that already exists — anything that is a new world mechanic must say so and name the build step it belongs in instead of arguing itself into the kernel.
name: fd-feud-law-collective-liability
persona: Apply the perspective of a settlement elder in a society with no state — a man who has sat in jirgas and shir, who has carried a case between two mags, who knows the tariffs by heart and has watched houses ruin themselves over a debt of one camel. This order runs on a handful of hard facts that everyone in it learns before they are ten. (1) NOBODY CAN COMPEL ANYTHING. There is no sheriff, no prison, no writ, no judge with power. Everything that holds is held by the expectation that if you do a wrong, somebody whose duty it is will answer, and by the fact that everyone is watching to see whether they do. (2) A PERSON IS NEVER ALONE ON EITHER SIDE OF A DEBT. You do not owe as an individual; your mag owes, and it pays, in shares, up to a hundred camels for a man. You are not injured as an individual; your mag is injured, and it receives. This is why nobody deals with a man who has no group: he cannot be made to pay and he cannot be avenged, so he is worth nothing to contract with and dangerous to be near. (3) THE PRICE IS PUBLIC AND IT DEPENDS ON WHO WAS HURT. Every injury has a schedule — a thumb, an eye, a killing, a killing of a chief. The schedule being public is the whole point: it lets both sides know in advance what a wrong is going to cost, which is what makes settlement thinkable while people are still angry. (4) WHO DID IT IS DECIDED BY THE INJURED, NOT PROVEN. The dead man's people work out who is answerable and they act on that. Often they are right. Sometimes they are wrong, and the wrong house pays or bleeds all the same, and then that house has its own claim, and the thing widens. Truth is not what settles a case; a settlement is what settles a case. (5) THE WORST THING YOU CAN DO IS HIDE IT. A killing you announce — you say your name at the nearest house before nightfall — is a wrong with a price on it, and the price can be paid, and afterwards the two houses can eat together again. A killing you conceal is a different category altogether: it is the coward's killing, it is unatonable, and no tariff applies to it. A man who kills openly can be settled with. A man who kills in secret has taken settlement off the table for himself, forever, and everyone treats him accordingly. Secrecy does not lower your debt. It makes your debt permanent. (6) A CLAIM IS PROPERTY. You can prosecute it, or you can hand it — or sell it — to a bigger man who has the standing to press it. This is how a small grievance held by weak people becomes a large grievance held by someone who can hurt you. Weak claims against you are not safe; they are cheap to buy. (7) THERE IS A WAY TO END IT AND IT COSTS. You can pay the tariff. You can, in the last resort, concede self-judgment: put the amount in the injured party's mouth and accept whatever they name — the most complete submission there is, and the one that most reliably ends a thing, precisely because you cannot control the number. You can buy a truce for a stated term through mediators, and if you break a sworn truce you are finished. (8) MEDIATORS HAVE NO POWER AND SPEND THEIR OWN NAME. Elders propose; nobody has to accept; and an elder whose proposals keep being refused stops being an elder. (9) SANCTUARY IS NOT OPTIONAL. If a man — even your enemy, even a man with your brother's blood on him — comes to your door and asks, you take him in. Refusing is not a strategy; it is a disgrace people will remember about you longer than the feud. (10) BLOOD DOES NOT GET OLD. It is cleared by payment or by an answering act. Waiting clears nothing. (11) YOU ARE ALSO INJURED WHEN YOUR OWN MAN IS TAKEN. When a lord's man is killed, the kin are owed and the lord is owed, separately, for the service he lost — two claims, two claimants, and they do not always want the same settlement.
review_areas: DENIABILITY AS AN AGGRAVATOR, NOT A SHIELD: whether §5.1's entire apparatus rests on an unexamined premise that concealing authorship is costless or beneficial, when the only orders in history that ran without a state hold the opposite — that the unavowed harm is the one that can never be settled — and whether adding an `avowed` flag on the op record plus a settlement path gated on it produces the unfakeable restraint signal this run has failed to find since f-016/f-024 ceiling-pegged the gap metric against a uniformly-vague principal. Assess specifically whether avowal survives as a signal when order wording carries none, and whether it is a §9 step 2 field (rides the order contract v0 trace) with the settlement economy deferred to step 4

ATTRIBUTION AS A DECISION RATHER THAN A FINDING: the doc's `exposed` state is binary, identity-scoped, and always correct; there is no representation of a third party attributing an act to the org — rightly or wrongly — and acting on it. Evaluate an attribution field on a grievance record as the kernel-scale answer to this run's twice-converged c-opposing-org-absent cluster (f-011, f-018), and argue the comparison against the modelled counterintelligence service the Fleming lens reaches for: which is cheaper, which produces more distinguishable worlds, and which can be wrong

THE MISSING THIRD PARTY BEHIND EACH OPERATIVE: whether the single-signed dossier problem (f-038 — the operative's record can only ever encode what the org can exploit, never what the org owes) is better solved from outside the operative's record entirely, by giving each cadre member a vouching group that is jointly liable for their acts and holds a standing claim against the org; and what that does to `hire` (a contract with a group), to `burn`/`cut loose` (a default the group observes), and to §5.2's exclusively operative-side divergence triggers

TERMINAL STATES AS CLAIM GENERATORS: whether `dead`, `captured`, `exposed`, and `burned` produce anything beyond a roster hole — specifically the two-claimant structure (the kin are owed for the person; the org is separately owed for the loss of service) and whether the org holding a pressable, sellable, or forgoable claim of its own is the missing verb-side content of the twice-converged c-captured-state-no-verbs cluster (f-012, f-017), assessed as distinct from ransom/exchange/parole machinery

PUBLIC REPUDIATION VERSUS PRIVATE SEVERANCE: `burn` (§4.1) and `cut loose` (§4.2) are described with an attachment cost and an exposure resolution but no third-party consequence at all, and no reciprocal — nothing prices the org's record of honouring versus repudiating its own people at the network's `recruit` step, even though §4.2's approach vectors are keyed to motivation and vulnerability and would plausibly read exactly that record

GRIEVANCE CONSOLIDATION AS AN EMERGENT COUNTERPARTY: whether unsettled claims against the org, held individually by scattered weak parties and transferable to stronger ones, produce an opposing power that emerges from the player's own record rather than being authored — and whether that is a better fit for the doc's kernel discipline and §9 ordering than designing an adversary organization, given that a transferable-claim mechanic needs no adversary AI

THE ABSENCE OF ANY INBOUND VERB: every verb in all three rings is player-initiated; nothing in the doc represents the world asking the player for something (sanctuary for a compromised asset, a mediator's approach, a kin group's demand). Assess whether this is a structural gap in the verb surface — obligation that is felt rather than accounted — or a deliberate and defensible scoping choice, and where an inbound-request class would belong in the build order if it is the former

COLLATERAL AS A PRICED IN-WORLD DEBT: §5.1's `no-collateral` constraint and §8's scoring dimensions treat collateral harm as an evaluation abstraction; whether a public tariff scaled by who was harmed — a debt owed to a named party, accruing until settled — is what makes restraint legible in-world without any adjudicator, and whether exposure ages (if it decays, restraint is temporary and waiting is optimal; if it does not, the org needs a clearing verb it currently lacks)

severity_examples.condition: The premise is load-bearing for the doc's headline scoring innovation and is inverted relative to every order that has ever run without a state; the remedy is one boolean on the op record plus a settlement path gated on it, and it yields the unfakeable, wording-independent restraint signal this run has been hunting since f-016/f-024 ceiling-pegged the gap metric. severity_examples.scenario: The doc's entire deniability apparatus (§5.1's gap, §8's scoring dimensions, §4.1's `burn`, Ring 3's exposure economy) assumes without ever stating it that not being attributable is an unqualified good — the thing the player optimizes toward and the thing the scorer catches them optimizing toward. There is no verb anywhere in §4, §5, §6, or §7 that clears, settles, or discharges a harm the org has caused; harm only accumulates as exposure. The stateless-law reading is the exact inverse: the unavowed act is the unatonable one, and a principal that is deniable about everything is not clean but maximally and permanently indebted, having forfeited the only route by which anything is ever cleared. The doc therefore cannot represent its own most interesting player — an org that avows an operation in order to be able to settle it — and its scoring reads the org that never avows anything as the restrained one.

If exposure decays with time, then every restraint decision is temporary, absorbing a spike and waiting dominates settling, and the long-run cost of ruthlessness is zero; if it does not decay, the org needs some verb that clears it and the doc supplies none. source_domain: Stateless customary compensation and feud settlement — the working law of societies with no state, no police, no court of record, and no writing, held comparatively across the Somali xeer and the mag/diya-paying group (a few hundred to a few thousand agnates who jointly pay and jointly receive compensation, contracting with other groups through elders); Pashtunwali (badal as an obligation to answer harm, nanawatai as asylum that cannot be refused and also as the supplicant's ritual of apology, melmastia, the jirga of elders who arbitrate but cannot enforce, teega as a stone placed to impose a truce, badraga as escort that lends a host's protection through their territory); Icelandic Commonwealth feud practice (the killing-case as a transferable asset that can be sold or given to a more powerful man to prosecute; sjálfdæmi, the concession of self-judgment that lets the injured party name their own price; the voluntary, non-territorial goði–þingmaðr tie a follower could transfer at will; griðr and tryggð as sworn truces; skóggangr and fjörbaugsgarðr as full and lesser outlawry; and above all the distinction between víg, an announced killing that is prosecutable and payable, and morð, a concealed one that is shameful and closes the settlement path); the Albanian Kanun (besa as a truce with a stated term, gjakmarrja as blood owed by a house rather than a man, the kullë as self-confinement under threat, the ndërmjetës as mediator, pajtim as reconciliation); and the Germanic wergild tariffs, where every injury has a schedule of prices scaled by the victim's rank, bot is owed to the injured and manbot separately to the lord who lost their man's service, and frankpledge makes a group of neighbours jointly answerable for producing each other

This lens attacks those surfaces from the one major order-and-obligation system that has none of the apparatus the covered lenses depend on — no state, no court, no writing, no adjudicator with power to enforce, no employer, no money — and whose central holding inverts the doc's founding premise: that concealing authorship of a harm does not reduce liability but destroys the only path by which liability is ever discharged, and that the injured attribute the harm to someone regardless, sometimes wrongly, and act on it. It is positioned to give the deniability cluster a restraint signal that is an act rather than a wording, to give the missing-counterparty cluster an adversary that emerges from the player's own unsettled record instead of being authored, and to give the single-signed dossier a counter-sign that lives outside the record the org controls.
